How cities are rethinking the commute

Bus lanes, bike corridors and four-day weeks are changing how millions of people get to work.

By A. Writer · 6 min read
Illustration

When the morning rush stopped being a rush, transport planners got an unexpected chance to experiment. Streets that had been built for one peak hour now carry traffic spread across the day.

ADVERTISEMENT

Several cities used the moment to repaint lanes, retime signals and test fare-free routes. The early results suggest that small, cheap changes can move more people than large projects that take a decade to finish.

Planners say the next step is data that respects riders' privacy: counting trips without following individual people from stop to stop.
